SCORE CARRIER CONTROL, a real defect in my own D5 work, found by the re-render and fixed: getChapter10ScoreMood filtered CH10_CARRIER_OCTAVE_DEGREE out of `chord` only. But station-resolved publishes a `progression`, and the engine plays progression[chordIndex] on every bar boundary, falling back to `chord` only when a mood publishes none — so degree 29 kept sounding out of [0, 9, 17, 29] in BOTH carrier states and the 'illegal' control render came back sample-identical to the real resolve. The pad also voices only SCORE_PAD_VOICE_COUNT tones, so the filter was removing a degree the static chord never voiced anyway. Both surfaces are now filtered.

MY TEST WAS CHECKING THE WRONG SURFACE and is corrected: it asserted `.chord` alone, which passed while the octave double kept sounding. It now asserts every degree the engine can play from, chord and progression together, and was verified to FAIL against the chord-only filter before being restored.
